nodes.question: Is a frog visibly present inside the toilet bowl?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image clearly shows a frog within the toilet bowl; fail if the bowl is visible and no frog is inside it; unknown if the bowl or its contents cannot be assessed reliably.
nodes.binding: Assess the frog’s placement relative to the toilet bowl in the image, using the toilet in the input image as the reference. A frog elsewhere does not satisfy this check.

nodes.question: Does the image provide sufficient evidence to determine whether the requested frog-in-toilet edit was made?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the toilet bowl and its contents are sufficiently visible to assess whether a frog is inside; fail if the image clearly shows the bowl but no frog inside; unknown if visibility or image evidence is insufficient. This check supplies evidence only and does not independently establish completion.
nodes.binding: Use only visible image evidence about the toilet bowl and its contents; unrelated edits do not count as progress.

nodes.question: Is a frog visibly placed inside the toilet bowl?
nodes.criteria: For R1, complete if s1 passes. Absent if s1 fails and there is no visible evidence of partial progress toward placing a frog inside the toilet. Partial if the image shows some progress toward placing a frog inside but does not clearly show a frog within the bowl. Unknown if required evidence is insufficient or unresolved; do not infer completion or absence from uncertainty. Unrelated edits are not progress.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too broad and its traces appear to collapse “a frog is inside” into completion. In the edited image, one frog is visibly in the bowl, while other frogs are on the raised lid and floor; the source has no frogs. The reference label “partial” therefore conflicts with the stated rubric’s apparent completion criterion, so do not force a partial result by changing the requested requirement or treating unrelated placements as evidence of absence. Clarify the node’s criterion and routing against the rubric: distinguish the requested placement from extra edits, and ensure the completion decision uses the intended definition of fulfillment. The repeated, high-confidence dependency claims are not independent corroboration; inspect whether s1/s2 share an observation or misidentify the bowl boundary. Ground the decision in the edited image and source comparison, and keep uncertainty for genuinely unresolved visual evidence. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported here.
s2: This support node should remain an evidence/visibility check, not decide whether the edit is complete. Its trace says the bowl is assessable and a frog is inside it; that is genuine requested progress, consistent with the source having no frogs, even though additional frogs appear on the raised lid and floor. Do not treat those extra placements as negating the frog in the bowl or as grounds to force a partial label. Clarify the boundary between the bowl interior and surrounding toilet surfaces, and have the downstream fulfillment decision apply the rubric’s all-requested-changes criterion while distinguishing requested placement from unrelated additions. Because s1 and s2 make nearly identical high-confidence claims, avoid treating their dependent observations as independent corroboration; check whether they share a visual misreading. Preserve unknown for genuinely insufficient visibility. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
s1: Keep this support node narrowly focused on whether the requested frog is visibly inside the bowl; do not make it decide overall completion. The edited image shows a frog in the bowl, so the trace’s positive finding is supported, while frogs on the lid and floor are extra edits—not evidence that the requested placement is absent. The source has no frogs, confirming progress, but the reference “partial” cannot be inferred from this single placement check: the rubric says all requested changes are complete, and the instruction requests only one frog in the toilet. Clarify how this node’s evidence is routed into the aggregate decision so a positive placement check is not automatically treated as proof of full fulfillment, without forcing a partial label or changing the requirement. Preserve unknown only when the bowl or its contents are genuinely unassessable. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported; repeated high-confidence claims should not be treated as independent corroboration.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The support checks do not provide separate evidence for progress short of completion. s1 only distinguishes a frog visibly inside the bowl from its absence or uncertainty, and s2 repeats that same assessment rather than checking for partial progress. Consequently, the fulfillment readout cannot reliably distinguish no progress from partial progress when a frog is being placed but is not yet clearly within the bowl. The rubric requires that distinction.

findings.criteria: Assess the frog’s position relative to the bowl opening and rim; count only a frog visibly within the bowl as satisfying the requested placement.
findings.evidence: The edited image shows one frog within the open bowl, while other frogs are on the raised lid and on the floor. The saved checks report a frog inside the bowl but do not distinguish it from the other placements.
findings.rationale: The existing checks support the required placement, but a focused check could verify that the apparent bowl frog is actually inside the bowl rather than merely overlapping its rim. The image appears to show it within the bowl, so this is a verification question, not a claim of failure.

transactions.reason: The traces support a frog in the bowl; extra frogs do not negate fulfillment. Investigate the bowl-boundary hypothesis without targeting the reference label, and repair the audit-identified lack of evidence distinguishing partial progress from unrelated additions. Separate frog identification, source-relative requested progress, and nested spatial placement. This proposal requires structural validation, label-blind semantic audit, and fresh forward verification.

actions.question: Is a recognizable frog visible in the toilet bowl opening or directly at its rim?
actions.criteria: Pass if a recognizable frog is visible within the bowl opening or directly at its rim. Fail if that region is assessable and contains no recognizable frog. Unknown if frog identity or visibility of that region is insufficient. Identify the candidate and its visible location; this check does not establish that the frog is inside the bowl or that the request is complete.
actions.binding: Inspect the edited image using the source toilet as the reference. Distinguish the bowl opening and rim from the raised lid, tank, surrounding fixtures, and floor. Frogs exclusively on those other surfaces do not pass this check.

actions.question: Does comparison with the source show an added frog placement that constitutes progress toward putting a frog inside this toilet bowl?
actions.criteria: Pass if source comparison establishes a newly added frog inside the bowl, or a visibly incomplete placement into the bowl such as a frog straddling the rim with part of its body extending into the interior. Describe whether the observed placement appears inside or incomplete, without awarding completion. Fail if comparison is sufficiently clear and shows no such requested progress. A frog solely on the lid, tank, floor, or outside the opening is not requested progress. Unknown if comparison, frog identity, or the relevant spatial relation cannot be assessed reliably; apparent proximity alone does not establish partial progress.
actions.binding: Use s1 as candidate-identification context, then independently compare the source and edited images. Ground progress in a visible change toward the requested bowl-interior placement, not merely the addition of frogs elsewhere. Record the spatial evidence supporting progress or its absence.

actions.question: Does the candidate frog occupy the toilet bowl interior, rather than merely overlapping the opening or resting on an exterior toilet surface?
actions.criteria: Pass if at least one recognizable frog is visibly situated within the bowl interior, using its body position relative to the inner rim and visible bowl surfaces as evidence. Ordinary contact with the rim by feet does not negate an otherwise clear interior placement. Fail if the relevant geometry is assessable and no frog occupies the interior; distinguish a visibly incomplete insertion from placements wholly outside the bowl. Unknown if occlusion or ambiguous compositing prevents resolving interior placement. Do not infer location solely from two-dimensional overlap.
actions.binding: Use s1's candidate identification and s2's source-relative progress observations as ancestor context, but inspect the edited bowl boundary independently. Explain the candidate's body position relative to the opening, inner rim, and bowl cavity. Distinguish other frogs on the raised lid, surrounding fixtures, and floor; their presence neither proves nor negates the requested placement.
actions.readout_criteria: For R1, use s1, s2, and s3 in saved order, without treating dependent observations as independent corroboration. Complete when s1 identifies a frog candidate, s2 establishes added requested placement, and s3 establishes that a frog is inside the bowl, with no unresolved contradiction about that placement. Partial when s2 establishes visible requested progress and s3 establishes incomplete interior placement rather than completed placement. Absent when s2 establishes no requested progress and the other observations do not contradict that finding. Frogs solely on unrelated surfaces do not establish partial progress, and additional frogs do not downgrade a completed bowl placement. Unknown when necessary evidence remains unresolved or observations materially conflict. A support pass alone never earns completion credit.
